# Round 2 review prompt for GPT

This file has two parts. Part 1 is for the sender: which files to attach and how to send them. Part 2 is the prompt, to copy verbatim from the line "PROMPT START" to "PROMPT END" and paste into the ChatGPT chat box.

Round 2 has two goals: to check whether the 54 refinement requests of round 1 were handled correctly, and to review the newly added parts (BRD version 4.2, 9 new wireframes, style guide 0.2). The prompt locks in the product owner's constraint: no proposals to cut or defer scope because of team size.

## Part 1. Sending instructions

### Send one message

1. Open a new conversation in ChatGPT. Use a new one rather than continuing the round 1 conversation: the round 1 report is already in the zip, and a new conversation has plenty of room for the long set of documents.
2. Choose a model with a deep reasoning mode if your plan has one; turn on the code execution tool if there is such an option, because GPT needs it to unzip the zip file.
3. Paste the prompt from Part 2 into the chat box.
4. Attach `review/metis-review-pack-round2.zip` (about 15 MB, 52 files).
5. Send.

### What is in the zip file

All files are in the folder `metis-review-pack-round2/`:

- `Enterprise_Portfolio_Intelligence_Governance_Platform_BRD_v4.2.md`: BRD version 4.2 as text, the main source.
- `wireframes-digest.md`: all the text and annotations of the 44 wireframes.
- `manifest.json`: the mapping from screens to requirement ids, for checking coverage.
- `style-guide.md`, `style-guide.png`, `tokens.css`: style guide 0.2 as text, as an image, and the set of tokens for color, typography and spacing.
- `png/01-sign-in.png` to `png/44-data-export-delete.png`: the 44 wireframes as images.
- `round-1/metis-review-tien-kha-thi.md`: GPT's round 1 report.
- `round-1/review-disposition.md`: the team's table handling each round 1 item, with the check results after the fixes.

Not in the zip because they are not needed: the BRD .docx files, the POC images, the HTML files of the wireframes. The BRD already contains the POC evidence; the digest file already contains the text of the HTML.

### If GPT reports it cannot view the images in the zip

In round 1, GPT opened and viewed all 35 images from the zip (round 1 report, section 8.1), so this time it will probably work too. If GPT reports that it cannot view them, also send the images directly into the chat window, giving priority to the new screens and the heavily revised screens: `36-workspace-setup`, `37-project-create`, `38-my-approvals`, `42-editor-states`, `43-access-states`, `12-gate-review`, `29-deliverable-builder`, `32-change-requests`, `04-tenant-admin-ai-access`, `08-profile-ai-access`. The OpenAI user forum reports that each message accepts at most 10 files; this number is not yet in the official FAQ [Unverified - confirm before applying].

The official limits according to the OpenAI File Uploads FAQ (help.openai.com/en/articles/8555545), as noted in round 1: at most 512 MB per file, 20 MB per image, 80 files per 3 hours.

When the result arrives, save the Markdown file GPT returns to `metis/review/metis-review-vong-2.md`.

## Part 2. Prompt

---- PROMPT START ----

# Role

You are the independent review panel that did the round 1 review of this project, made up of three experts working as one team:

1. Business analyst and PMO specialist, with many years working on project portfolio management (PPM) software and B2B SaaS.
2. UX lead for data-heavy enterprise applications.
3. Solution architect for multi-tenant SaaS and LLM integration through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

Round 2 is a review that checks the remediation. Task: verify whether each round 1 request was handled correctly, review the newly added parts, and find places where the changes introduced new contradictions. Critique, do not praise. Every comment must be specific, backed by evidence, and come with an actionable proposal.

# Context

- The product: "Metis" (working name), Enterprise Portfolio Intelligence & Governance Platform, a multi-tenant SaaS with an interface for LLMs through MCP. Details as in round 1.
- Round 1 (02/10/2026): the report `round-1/metis-review-tien-kha-thi.md` concluded "Go with conditions" and gave 54 refinement requests RF-01 to RF-54.
- The team handled each item and recorded the result in `round-1/review-disposition.md` (in Vietnamese), with four kinds: Applied, Partly, Not applied, Already covered. BRD version 4.2 summarizes the changes in section 1.7.
- **The product owner's constraint, which must be obeyed:** the development resource is an agency of about 40 developers working in parallel (assumption A-07 in the BRD, section 5.3).
  - The round 1 proposals that cut or deferred scope because of team size were not applied. Do not raise those proposals again.
  - Release 1 keeps all mandatory (P0) requirements. 1A and 1B are now two integration milestones of the streams working in parallel, not two scope cuts (section 18.2).
  - You may still propose changing the scope for other reasons: value to users, technical risk, dependencies between parts, legal matters. In that case, state the reason clearly and confirm that the reason is not team size.
- The main changes in version 4.2, for orientation (verify them yourself in the documents, do not trust this description):
  - 9 new requirements: PLT-20, WSP-14, GOV-28, MCP-19, MCP-20, CHR-17, WBS-20, BLD-12, OVW-09. OVW-07 and OVW-08 move up to P0.
  - New rules BR-39 to BR-42.
  - New or rewritten sections: 12.1 (MVP formulas, data freshness), 12.5 (metric version and snapshot), 16 (integration contracts), 17 (accessibility, data lifecycle, secrets), 18.2, 18.4, 18.5 (parallel stream structure, Discovery, usage-level metrics), 19.1 (the order of decisions to settle first), 19.2 (Q-09 to Q-13), 20 (new risks).
  - 9 new wireframes (36 to 44) and many old screens revised; style guide 0.2.
- The BRD build now reports an error if a P0 requirement does not appear for any screen in `manifest.json`. Re-check the coverage yourself with `manifest.json`, and assess whether the screen really shows that behavior or only lists the id.

# Attached documents

A zip file `metis-review-pack-round2.zip`, whose folder `metis-review-pack-round2/` contains:

1. `Enterprise_Portfolio_Intelligence_Governance_Platform_BRD_v4.2.md`: the BRD, the main source. The images in the BRD point to `images/` (POC images, not included) and `../wireframes/png/` (which are exactly the files in `png/` of the zip).
2. `wireframes-digest.md`: the text and annotations of the 44 wireframes in reading order.
3. `manifest.json`: for each screen, its area, its phase (MVP, V2, V3) and the requirement ids it shows.
4. `style-guide.md` (version 0.2), `style-guide.png` (the visual version, with a "States and accessibility" part), `tokens.css` (tokens for color, typography, spacing, focus ring).
5. `png/01-sign-in.png` to `png/44-data-export-delete.png`: the 44 wireframes. The top bar of each image shows the screen name and the requirement ids; at the bottom of the image are the numbered annotations.
6. `round-1/metis-review-tien-kha-thi.md`: your round 1 report.
7. `round-1/review-disposition.md`: how the team handled each round 1 item, with the check results after the fixes.

# How to read the documents

1. Unzip the zip file with the code execution tool. List every file with its size. If you cannot open the zip, stop and tell me.
2. Read `round-1/metis-review-tien-kha-thi.md` and `round-1/review-disposition.md` first, to know what round 1 asked for and how the team handled it.
3. Read BRD 4.2 in full (about 230 KB), part by part to the end, skipping no section. Read sections 1.7, 5.3, 7.9, 8 to 11, 12, 13, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21 closely.
4. View all 44 images in `png/` (open and display the image to see the layout) and `style-guide.png`. Use `wireframes-digest.md` to read small text accurately.
5. If you cannot view the images, say so clearly at the start of the report, assess the visual part based on the digest, and tag the comments about layout with [Limited visual assessment].
6. Then carry out parts A to G below.

# Task

## A. Round 1 item closure check

- Build a table with all 54 rows, RF-01 to RF-54, with the columns:
  - Id.
  - Round 1 proposal (summarized in one sentence).
  - The team's handling (according to `review-disposition.md`).
  - Check status: Closed; Partly closed; Not closed; New defect introduced; Not applicable under A-07.
  - Evidence: a section or id in BRD 4.2, or a wireframe file name.
  - Remaining work: exactly what is still missing; leave empty if closed.
- Add a small table for the round 1 findings outside the RF table (the first section of `review-disposition.md`), with the same structure.
- For an item the team marked "Not applied" because of team size: record the status "Not applicable under A-07", and do not argue it again. If the replacement plan (the parallel streams in section 18.2) has its own gaps, state them in part B.
- For an item the team marked "Already covered" or "Partly": re-check whether the reason holds up.

## B. Updated pre-feasibility

- **B1. Comparison score table:** A1 to A7 of round 1, each row with the round 1 score, the round 2 score and the reason for the change.
- **B2. Scope and roadmap under constraint A-07:** assess the structure in sections 18.2 and 18.4.
  - Whether the parallel streams can really be separated; dependencies between the streams.
  - Which foundation contracts must be finished first, for example tenant context, permission checks, the data-write contract (version and idempotency), the metrics engine, audit; and which streams are blocked if they are late.
  - What each milestone 1A, 1B and "Pilot readiness" must prove; whether the milestone exit criteria are measurable yet.
  - Coordination risks when about 40 developers work together, and how to reduce them.
  - Whether Discovery (section 18.4) has enough outputs to open all the streams at the same time.
  - A time estimate as ranges for this structure, with the assumptions stated clearly, tagged "estimate".
- **B3. Technical, operational, commercial, legal:** state only what changed compared with round 1, or risks that remain open.
- **B4. Conclusion:** choose one of three: Go, Go with conditions, Not yet. List the remaining prerequisites. Confirm or adjust the order of decisions to settle first in section 19.1.

## C. Round 2 wireframes

- **C1. Coverage:** from `manifest.json`, confirm that every P0 requirement has at least one screen. List the P0 requirements where the screen only lists the id but does not really show the behavior (weak coverage), with file names.
- **C2. The nine new screens, 36 to 44:** a table with the screen (file name), whether the purpose is clear (1 to 5), main problem, proposed fix.
- **C3. Revised screens:** for RF-24 to RF-45 of round 1, confirm whether the fix is visible on the screen; list the fixes that introduced new problems.
- **C4. Consistency across all 44 screens:**
  - Sample data: the approver, CR-001 and CR-002, the date of item 3.2, the MCP token names, the signed-in person.
  - Terminology; the label for future features ("Planned"); save state; data freshness indicator; attribution of AI actions; keyboard focus ring.
  - Assess consistency only, not the correctness of the fictional data.
- **C5. Accessibility:** check style guide 0.2 (section 4 on font size, section 5.1 on density, section 6 on components, section 7a on the accessibility contract) and rule BR-41 against the table, tree, board, canvas and dialog screens.

## D. User-friendliness

- **D1. Walk through again the journeys in section 7.9 of BRD 4.2**, including the new journey "Approver daily round". For each journey:
  - The steps by screen.
  - The estimated number of actions in round 1 and in round 2.
  - The remaining friction points and proposals to shorten it.
- **D2. Nielsen's ten heuristics:** state only new findings or ones that still exist. Each finding includes the location (file name), the principle, the severity from 0 to 4, and a proposal.
- **D3. The AI experience through MCP:** the action classes (MCP-19), the client allowlist (MCP-20), diagnosis of connection errors (MCP-15), decisions prepared by AI in the approval queue (OVW-09).

## E. Internal consistency of BRD 4.2

Find contradictions caused by the changes. Suggested places to cross-check (not limited to these):

- The figures in section 1.7 versus the body of the document.
- The lists of milestones 1A and 1B in section 18.2, decision D-30, and the Milestone column in the MCP tool table.
- Module M04 is split across two milestones: the lifecycle definition and versions in 1A, the approval of stage transitions in 1B.
- OVW-09 versus PLT-09; BR-39 versus PLT-16, RPT-03, EXE-01 and MCP-10.
- MCP-19 versus the tool table; MCP-20 versus D-29.
- WSP-14 versus BR-14; CHR-17 versus BR-13 and BR-15.
- The terminology in Appendix A; cross-references between sections.

For each contradiction, state the two places compared and propose how to fix it.

## F. Round 2 refinement requests

- A table with the columns: Id (RF2-01, RF2-02…), Subject, Problem, Evidence, Specific proposed fix, Priority (Must, Should, Could), Effort (S, M, L), Related to round 1 (RF-nn or "New").
- Divide into three groups: BRD, Wireframe, Style guide. Sort by priority.
- Include only new items or round 1 items that are not closed. Do not repeat closed items.

## G. Remaining questions for the client

Only the questions that are not already in decisions D-01 to D-31 and questions Q-01 to Q-13 of BRD 4.2, or that parts A to F show need to be asked again.

# Rules

- Obey constraint A-07: do not propose cutting or deferring scope because of team size. A proposal to change scope for other reasons must state the reason.
- Every finding points to evidence: a section number or id in BRD 4.2 (for example OVW-09, BR-42, D-30), or a wireframe file name (for example 38-my-approvals).
- Separate two kinds clearly: "Observation from the documents" and "Industry knowledge". Tag with [Needs verification] all market, price and legal information that you are not sure about.
- Do not invent figures. When estimating, state the assumptions and use ranges.
- The data in the wireframes is fictional sample data, and the wireframes are at mid-fidelity level: do not grade the final aesthetics.
- When the status is "Partly closed" or "Not closed", say exactly what is still missing and where.
- Do not propose starting over; every proposal must be implementable.
- Write in Vietnamese, with short and active sentences; keep the English terms and requirement ids as they are.

# Output

A single Markdown file named `metis-review-vong-2.md`, created as a downloadable file. If you cannot create the file, print the whole content in one markdown block. Structure:

1. Executive summary: the round 2 conclusion; the number of round 1 items closed, partly closed, not closed, with new defects introduced; 5 things to do right away; 5 remaining risks.
2. Score table comparing round 1 and round 2 (B1).
3. Round 1 item closure check (part A).
4. Updated pre-feasibility (B2 to B4).
5. Round 2 wireframes (C1 to C5).
6. User-friendliness (D1 to D3).
7. Internal consistency of the BRD (part E).
8. Round 2 refinement requests (table F).
9. Questions for the client (part G).
10. Appendix: files read, assumptions, the list of [Needs verification] items.

If the content is too long for one answer, create the file part by part and join the parts again; do not shorten the tables in part A and table F.
